# Data sources

- [Description](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-026-07901-0#additional-information)
- [Download](https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/ROP-VL_An_Open_Dataset_Integrating_Fundus_Photograph_and_Clinical_Knowledge_for_Retinopathy_of_Prematurity/30143461/1?file=58329352)

# What is ROP?

Retinopathy of prematurity is an eye disease affecting premature infants  
where abnormal blood vessels grow in the retina,  
potentially leading to retinal detachment and vision loss.  

# Normal

healthy; no findings; no lesion signs;  
no retinopathy; incomplete vascularization.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
norm_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="normal",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in norm_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# Stage 1

a thin white line at the vascular-avascular junction  
with possible abnormal vessel branching.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
st1_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="Stage 1 ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in st1_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# Stage 2

ridge with width and height that evolves from the demarcation line;  
the ridge may vary in height; the ridge's color ranges from white to pink;  
small isolated tufts of neovascular tissue lying on the surface of the retina;  
ridge is raised and thicker than stage 1 ROP.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
st2_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="Stage 2 ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in st2_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# Stage 3

extraretinal neovascular proliferation extends from the ridge into the vitreous;  
is continuous with the posterior aspect of the ridge, causing a ragged appearance as  
proliferation becomes more extensive; Seemingly flat-appearing extraretinal neovascularization  
can occur in eyes with zone 1 or posterior zone 2 disease,in the absence  
of an obvious ridge or demarcation line.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
st3_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="Stage 3 ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in st3_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# Stage 4

partial retinal detachment, either spares  or involves the fovea;  
traction on extraretinal neovascularization leads to retinal elevation;  
tractional retinal detachment in the area of the peripheral ridge;  
detachment involving the macula; detachment with associated subretinal  
hemorrhage and lipid exudation into the macula; detachment of  
vascularized retina into a volcano shaped configuration.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
st4_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="Stage 4 ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in st4_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# Stage 5

total retinal detachment; open-funnel detachment, the optic disc is visible by ophthalmoscopy;  
closed-funnel detachment, the optic disc is not visible secondary;  
the optic disc is not visible secondary to retrolental fibrovascular tissue.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
st5_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="Stage 5 ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in st5_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# A-ROP (aggressive retinopathy of prematurity)

severe vasoconstriction; capillary nonperfusion; nonphysiologic dilated vascular loops;  
arteriovenous shunts; plus disease in zone 1; dilated vascular loops; diffuse flat  
extraretinal neovascularization most prominent superotemporally, and severe plus disease;  
flat extraretinal neovascularization with fibrosis, and early contraction superiorly;  
intraretinal and vitreous hemorrhage superotemporally; ill-defined junction between  
vascular and avascular retina in zone 1.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
A_ROP_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="A-ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in A_ROP_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

# Laser-treated ROP

laser scar; Laser spots look like small white dots on the retina,  
these are tiny burn marks; clear white retinal laser spots.  

```{r, echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,4),
    mar=c(0,0,0,0),
    oma=c(0,0,0,0))
LT_A_ROP_imgs <- lapply(imgs[imgs$label=="Laser-treated ROP",][1:8,2], load.image)
for (im in LT_A_ROP_imgs) plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
avg_color_single <- function(im) {
  # 1. Split the image into its R, G, and B channels
  R <- im[,,,1]
  G <- im[,,,2]
  B <- im[,,,3]
  
  # 2. Find pixels that are NOT pure black (where not all channels are 0)
  not_black_mask <- !(R == 0 & G == 0 & B == 0)
  
  # 3. Extract only the valid pixels for each channel
  valid_R <- R[not_black_mask]
  valid_G <- G[not_black_mask]
  valid_B <- B[not_black_mask]
  
  # 4. Calculate the mean of the non-black pixels
  mean_R <- mean(valid_R)
  mean_G <- mean(valid_G)
  mean_B <- mean(valid_B)
  
  return(c(Red = mean_R, Green = mean_G, Blue = mean_B))
}

avg_color_from_imgs <- function(imgs) {
  avg_color_ls <- lapply(imgs, avg_color_single)
  avg_color_df <- do.call(rbind, avg_color_ls)
  
  avg_color <- c(mean(norm_avg_color_df[,"Red"]),
                mean(norm_avg_color_df[,"Green"]),
                mean(norm_avg_color_df[,"Blue"]))
  
  return(avg_color)
}

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
avg_color_from_imgs(norm_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(st1_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(st2_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(st3_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(st4_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(st5_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(A_ROP_imgs)
avg_color_from_imgs(LT_A_ROP_imgs)
```
